title: Approximate Bayesian computation and summary-based inference

items.title: Approximate Bayesian computation and its tolerance-conditioned target
items.statement: For a proper prior and measurable simulator kernel, define the prior-predictive law of the parameter and summary and, when its event probability is positive, the indicator ABC target as the posterior conditioned on the summary falling in a specified Euclidean tolerance ball.
items.strategy: Push the prior-simulator joint law through the measurable summary map; normalize its restriction to the tolerance event only when the event has positive probability.

items.title: ABC rejection sampling
items.statement: Repeat independent prior draws and simulator draws; return the first parameter whose simulated summary lies in the observed-summary tolerance ball. The procedure is admissible only when the acceptance probability is positive.
items.strategy: Specify the proposal law, simulator call, measurable acceptance event, repeat rule, output, and positive-probability admissibility condition.

items.title: ABC rejection returns the tolerance-conditioned posterior
items.statement: If the tolerance event has probability p in (0,1], ABC rejection terminates almost surely and the accepted parameter has exactly the prior-predictive law conditioned on that event.
items.strategy: Partition the accepted output by its first successful proposal index; independence gives a geometric survival factor and a geometric-series normalization.

items.title: ABC targets the density-defined summary posterior at zero tolerance
items.statement: If the summary-predictive law has a specified jointly measurable density version continuous at the observed summary almost everywhere, positive finite prior-averaged density there, and an integrable envelope on a neighborhood, then the positive-tolerance ABC targets converge in total variation to the posterior selected by that density version.
items.strategy: Average the summary density over shrinking Euclidean balls, prove convergence in L1 by continuity and dominated convergence, normalize the averages, and bound the event-supremum total variation by their L1 difference.

items.title: A sufficient summary preserves the Bayesian posterior
items.statement: For standard-Borel data and summary spaces, a statistic sufficient through one parameter-independent conditional kernel makes the full-data posterior equal almost surely to a version depending only on the summary. In the stated dominated factorization form p_theta(y)=g(y)h_theta(S(y)), the explicit full-data and summary posterior densities agree wherever g and both finite-positive evidence normalizers permit the updates.
items.strategy: Mix the common conditional-data kernel over the prior to show the summary posterior composed with S satisfies the full-data conditional-law identities; then cancel the common factor g in the dominated Bayes formulas on good fibres.

title: Approximate Bayesian computation and simulation-based inference — Examples

items.title: Pointwise continuity alone does not guarantee the zero-tolerance limit
items.statement: Pointwise continuity of every summary density at the observed value and a positive finite prior-averaged density there do not suffice for total-variation convergence when no integrable local envelope controls the density spikes.
items.strategy: Use countably many continuous-at-zero densities with spikes at 1/n, a telescoping prior of order 1/n squared, and a sequence of shrinking balls whose posterior mass on one fixed parameter event has a limit different from its density-defined zero-tolerance mass.

items.title: An identifiable model can have persistent ABC summary distortion
items.statement: The claim that full-model identifiability alone makes every ABC summary target recover the full-data posterior is false.
items.strategy: Use two distinct point-mass sampling laws and a constant summary; the full-data posterior is a point mass while every tolerance event leaves the prior unchanged.

items.title: Vanishing acceptance probability with a stable zero-tolerance target
items.statement: With two equally likely parameter values and uniform simulator laws on adjacent unit intervals, the ABC acceptance probability for a half-width epsilon ball about 1/2 is epsilon for 0<epsilon<1/2, while the accepted parameter and density-defined zero-tolerance posterior are both the point mass at 0.
items.strategy: Compute the two interval intersection probabilities, average over the prior, and check the density regularity, normalizer, and limiting posterior directly.

items.title: A Bernoulli count is a sufficient summary for a finite-sample posterior
items.statement: For three Bernoulli observations, a two-point proper prior, and observed count two, the sample count is sufficient and ABC with any tolerance below one has the exact full-data posterior, with posterior masses 1/3 and 2/3.
items.strategy: Construct the common conditional kernel uniformly on each count fiber and compare the exact-sequence and count likelihoods; the common factor of three cancels.
